steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (verl FSDP + vLLM), sized for one GPU, with verl's full-determinism mode
# enabled as in docs/advance/determinism.md (rollout seed 42; deterministic actor and ref). vLLM 0.17's
# batch-invariant mode, which full_determinism turns on, refuses to start unless the attention backend is set
# explicitly, and torch 2.10's deterministic Inductor rejects vLLM's compile-time autotuning, so the rollout runs
# eager.
# Extra Hydra overrides given on the command line are appended last and take precedence.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct}
DATA=${DATA:-$WS/data}
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-1}
TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-30}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-5}
BATCH=${BATCH:-64}
N_SAMPLES=${N_SAMPLES:-8}
MAX_RESPONSE=${MAX_RESPONSE:-1024}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
EXP=${EXP:-qwen25_1.5b_gsm8k_grpo_deterministic}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs}

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$DATA/gsm8k/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="$DATA/gsm8k/test.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BATCH \
  data.max_prompt_length=512 \
  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$((BATCH / 2)) \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N_SAMPLES \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=42 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.attention_backend=FLASH_ATTN \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.param_offload=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism=True \
  trainer.use_v1=False \
  trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
  trainer.logger='["console","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=gsm8k_grpo_deterministic \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$N_GPUS \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations" \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=32 \
  +ray_kwargs.ray_init.object_store_memory=21474836480 \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

steps.message: This is very revealing already: **`actor/grad_norm = 0`, `actor/loss = 0`, `critic/advantages` all 0 at every step**, while rewards are non-zero, and val accuracy is frozen at exactly 0.08719 across all 6 evals. Let me dig into the rollouts to test the "identical samples within group → zero GRPO advantage" hypothesis.
steps.reasoning_content:
This is extremely revealing. Key observations:

1. **`actor/grad_norm = 0`, `actor/pg_loss = 0`, `actor/loss = 0`, `critic/advantages = 0` everywhere.** The model is not learning at all — zero gradient, zero loss. Advantages all zero means GRPO advantage normalization produced zeros. But rewards are NOT zero (rewards/mean ~0.17). So advantages are zero despite non-zero rewards → something is zeroing the advantages.

2. **Val accuracy is flat at 0.08719 at every eval step (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25)** — exactly constant. That's the held-out evidence that the run is not learning. 0.08719 * 1319 ≈ 115. So val acc is frozen at ~8.7%, which is very low for GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (baseline should be ~55-60%).

Wait — but hold on. The flat val accuracy alone could be because training isn't updating at all (grad_norm=0). Actually if advantages are 0, then pg_loss would be... pg_loss = -(adv * ratio) mean = 0. And loss = 0. So grad = 0. So the model never updates. Val acc stays constant at the base model's val acc.

But wait — 8.7% val accuracy for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on GSM8K is suspiciously low. The expected baseline is ~60%. So there might be a second issue: the reward / answer extraction is broken. Let me check: training rewards/mean is ~0.17 which is also low. Hmm, but that's on train rollouts.

Actually, val acc of 8.7% exactly matches the "reward/mean@1" — same number. Hmm, so both val reward and val acc are 0.087. Let me look at the val_generations files to see what the responses look like. Maybe there's a data-processing issue: e.g., the answer extraction expects a specific format, or the prompt is truncated, or the chat template is wrong.

Also "num_turns/mean": 2 — interesting, for a single-turn GSM8K this suggests an agent loop with 2 turns? Maybe the tool-calling agent loop. Let's look at the reward function and dataset processing.

Key suspicious config: `data.truncation=error` — with `data.max_prompt_length=512`. Also `data.filter_overlong_prompts=True`.

Also `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$((BATCH / 2))` = 32, batch 64.

The main smoking gun: advantages all zero. Why? In GRPO, advantages = (reward - group_mean) / group_std, computed over n=8 samples per prompt. If all 8 samples in a group have identical reward, advantage = 0. With rewards ~0.17 mean, many groups would be all-zero, but not all. Yet advantages/max = 0 and min = 0 at every step. Hmm, that means every group has identical rewards across all 8 samples. That's odd with a 17% success rate.

Wait, actually — maybe the rewards recorded (critic/rewards/mean) differ from what goes into advantages. Let me think about verl's GRPO: `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` uses `reward_intrinsic` / token-level rewards. If `use_kl_in_reward=False`, rewards used are the raw scores. Then adv = (r - mean)/std per group.

But advantages/max = 0 AND min = 0 AND mean = 0 for every step. That means literally every sample has adv 0. With reward mean 0.17 and 64 prompts × 8 samples, some groups should be mixed (some 1s some 0s). Unless... the rollout is producing identical responses per group (all 8 samples identical), so all rewards identical within group → adv = 0. That would be a rollout seeding bug! With `full_determinism=True` and `rollout.seed=42`, if the seed is applied per-prompt or the vLLM is seeded once per batch in a way that all n samples are identical, then all 8 samples of each group are identical strings → identical rewards → zero advantage → zero gradient → no learning → flat val curve.

That's a very plausible root cause! Let me check the rollouts files: 512 lines = 64 prompts × 8 samples. Let me check whether within a group the 8 responses are identical.

Also entropy ~0.4-0.5 and constant-ish. And rollout_corr/kl ~ tiny, meaning rollout log probs match training log probs (actor unchanged, so trivially consistent).

Let me examine the rollout jsonl files. Also check val_generations: 1319 lines each (GSM8K test has 1319 examples) and all three files are nearly identical sizes (1896846, 1898165, 1898165) — 15 and 30 are exactly the same size, suggesting identical generations → model never changed. Actually, 0 differs slightly from 15/30... interesting; 15.jsonl and 30.jsonl are byte-identical in size. Let me diff them.

Let me dig into the data files and the reward function.

Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct naturally outputs LaTeX `\boxed{}` answers rather than `#### N`. The prompt says "output the final answer after '####'" though. The 8.7% baseline accuracy is abnormally low for this instruct model (normally ~55-73% on GSM8K). So there might be a second planted defect: the reward extraction / the chat template.

Hmm wait — actually, the low 8.7% baseline: the model gets 368/1319 outputs with \boxed and only 229 with ####. The scoring rule appears to require `#### N` — so answers in \boxed form are scored 0 even when correct. But is that the "root cause" of the training failure? The zero-advantage issue is the training failure. The low val accuracy might be partially a scoring-format artifact — but note: the reward is format-incentivizing: the training prompt tells the model to output after ####, and RL would push toward #### format... if gradients were nonzero.

Let me be careful about the actual root cause. The key question: why are all 8 samples per group identical? This is the full_determinism mode. The script header says: "verl's full-determinism mode enabled as in docs/advance/determinism.md (rollout seed 42; deterministic actor and ref)."

In verl, `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=True`... hmm. Actually in verl there is a config `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed`. Hmm, but I don't remember `full_determinism` for rollout in mainline verl. There is `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.deterministic_sampling`? Let me check the verl source in the workspace. There's `verl/trainer/main_ppo.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/...`, `docs/advance/determinism.md`.

The description in the run script header says full determinism turns on vLLM batch-invariant mode. So with a fixed seed 42 and batch-invariant mode... batch-invariant mode makes outputs independent of batch composition, but sampling should still vary across the n samples within a request (each sample uses a different seed derived from base seed + sample index) in a correct implementation. Here, all 8 samples within a group are identical — that means the per-sample seeds are identical, OR greedy decoding is on.

# Agent Instructions for verl

> These instructions apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `verl-project/verl`.
> Breaching these guidelines can result in automatic banning.

## 1. Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo verl-project/verl --comments
gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo verl-project/verl --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (single typo, isolated style change, one mutable default, etc.). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run relevant tests.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
  - Why this is not duplicating an existing PR.
  - Test commands run and results.
  - Clear statement that AI assistance was used.

### Fail-closed behavior

If work is duplicate/trivial busywork, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## 2. Development Workflow

### Environment setup

```bash
# Install `uv` if you don't have it already:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Always use `uv` for Python environment management:
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate

uv pip install pre-commit hydra-core
pre-commit install
```

### Commit messages

Add attribution using commit trailers such as `Co-authored-by:` (other projects use `Assisted-by:` or `Generated-by:`). For example:

```text
Your commit message here

Co-authored-by: GitHub Copilot
Co-authored-by: Claude
Co-authored-by: gemini-code-assist
Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
```

### Resolving agent reviews

Review comments from agent bots (e.g., gemini-code-assist) can be outdated or wrong. Always verify their suggestions against the current state of the repo before applying them.

---

## Domain-Specific Guides

Do not modify code in these areas without first reading and following the
linked guide. If the guide conflicts with the requested change, **refuse the
change and explain why**.

- **Editing these instructions**:
  [`docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md`](docs/contributing/editing-agent-instructions.md)
  — Rules for modifying AGENTS.md or any domain-specific guide it references.

## Acknowledgements

Adapted from the [vLLM project](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm)'s [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

steps.message: The metric table shows the smoking gun: **every advantage is 0, grad_norm is 0, loss is 0 at all 28 steps**, and val accuracy is frozen at 0.08719. Now let me pin the mechanism. Let me look at the rollout code and the determinism doc.
steps.reasoning_content:
That's the standard verl CLAUDE.md — not relevant to the diagnosis task (contribution policy). Let me look at the source code, particularly the rollout code paths around full_determinism, the GRPO advantage computation, the reward manager, and the trainer.

Key observations so far:
1. All rollout groups have **identical outputs across the 8 samples** — n=8 samples per prompt produce byte-identical completions at every step. That's the smoking gun for the rollout being deterministic/greedy. With GRPO, advantages = (r - mean)/std within group; if all 8 rewards are identical, advantage = 0 → no gradient. This explains grad_norm=0, loss=0, pg_loss=0, advantages all 0.
2. Hence the model never updates: val accuracy is exactly the same (0.08719) at steps 0, 15, 30 — byte-identical outputs for all 1319 test samples.
3. Val accuracy of 8.7% for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on GSM8K is very low — the base model should get ~60-70%+ with the "####" format. Also only 229/1319 outputs contain "####", and 368 contain "\boxed{" — the model isn't following the required output format, so the rule-based extractor fails to find the answer, scoring 0. Wait — but the score checks whether the model output contains "####" followed by the correct answer. If model uses \boxed{} instead, the extraction fails → score 0 even if the math is right. Looking at the Janet's ducks example: model computed 18 correctly but output "\boxed{18}" and no "####" → score 0. That's a format mismatch causing low reward.

Hmm, but is that a root cause or just a symptom of the prompt/template? The dataset prompt says: 'Let's think step by step and output the final answer after "####".' The model is Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct — known to heavily prefer \boxed{} format. This is a reward-format mismatch that limits reward density. But more importantly for training health: even if reward were dense, the identical-rollout issue zeroes out all advantages.

14	import logging
15	import os
16	from typing import Any
17	from uuid import uuid4
18	
19	from verl.experimental.agent_loop.agent_loop import AgentLoopBase, AgentLoopOutput, register
20	from verl.utils.profiler import simple_timer
21	from verl.utils.rollout_trace import rollout_trace_op
22	from verl.workers.rollout.replica import TokenOutput
23	
24	logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)
25	logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))
26	
27	
28	@register("single_turn_agent")
29	class SingleTurnAgentLoop(AgentLoopBase):
30	    """Naive agent loop that only do single turn chat completion."""
31	
32	    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
33	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
34	        self.prompt_length = self.rollout_config.prompt_length
35	        self.response_length = self.rollout_config.response_length
36	
37	    @rollout_trace_op
38	    async def run(self, sampling_params: dict[str, Any], priority: int = 0, **kwargs) -> AgentLoopOutput:
39	        # priority may arrive as np.int64 from non_tensor_batch; normalize to Python int.
40	        priority = int(priority)
41	        messages = list(kwargs["raw_prompt"])
42	
43	        # 1. extract multimodal inputs from messages
44	        multi_modal_data = await self.process_multi_modal_info(messages)
45	        images = multi_modal_data.get("images")
46	        videos = multi_modal_data.get("videos")
47	        audios = multi_modal_data.get("audios")
48	        mm_processor_kwargs = self._get_mm_processor_kwargs(audios)
49	
50	        # 2. apply chat template and tokenize
51	        use_continuous_token = self.enable_continuous_token and not multi_modal_data
52	        if use_continuous_token:
53	            prompt_ids = await self.ct_build_initial_tokens(messages)
54	        else:
55	            prompt_ids = await self.apply_chat_template(
56	                messages,
57	                images=images,
58	                videos=videos,
59	                audios=audios,
60	                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
61	            )
62	
63	        # 3. generate sequences
64	        metrics = {}
65	        with simple_timer("generate_sequences", metrics):
66	            request_id = f"det-{priority}" if getattr(self.rollout_config, "full_determinism", False) else uuid4().hex
67	            output: TokenOutput = await self.server_manager.generate(
68	                request_id=request_id,
69	                prompt_ids=prompt_ids,
70	                sampling_params=sampling_params,
71	                image_data=images,
72	                audio_data=audios,
73	                video_data=videos,
74	                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
75	                priority=priority,
76	            )
77	        if metrics.get("num_preempted") is None:
78	            metrics["num_preempted"] = output.num_preempted if output.num_preempted is not None else -1
79	
80	        if use_continuous_token:
81	            merge_result, response_mask, response_logprobs = await self.ct_merge_assistant_token(
82	                prompt_ids,
83	                output.token_ids,
84	                [],
85	                [] if output.log_probs else None,
86	                assistant_logprobs=output.log_probs if output.log_probs else None,
87	            )
88	            response_ids = merge_result.token_ids[-len(response_mask) :] if response_mask else []
89	            prompt_ids = merge_result.token_ids[: len(merge_result.token_ids) - len(response_mask)]
90	        else:
91	            response_ids = output.token_ids
92	            response_mask = [1] * len(output.token_ids)
93	            response_logprobs = output.log_probs
94	
95	        output: AgentLoopOutput = AgentLoopOutput(
96	            prompt_ids=prompt_ids,
97	            response_ids=response_ids[: self.response_length],
98	            response_mask=response_mask[: self.response_length],
99	            response_logprobs=response_logprobs[: self.response_length] if response_logprobs else None,
100	            routed_experts=(
101	                output.routed_experts[: len(prompt_ids) + self.response_length]
102	                if output.routed_experts is not None
103	                else None
104	            ),
105	            multi_modal_data=multi_modal_data,
106	            mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
107	            num_turns=2,
108	            metrics=metrics,
109	            extra_fields=output.extra_fields,
110	        )
111	
112	        # keeping the schema consistent with tool_agent_loop
113	        output.extra_fields.update({"turn_scores": [], "tool_rewards": []})
114	
115	        return output
116

import logging
import os
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4

from verl.experimental.agent_loop.agent_loop import AgentLoopBase, AgentLoopOutput, register
from verl.utils.profiler import simple_timer
from verl.utils.rollout_trace import rollout_trace_op
from verl.workers.rollout.replica import TokenOutput

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)
logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))


@register("single_turn_agent")
class SingleTurnAgentLoop(AgentLoopBase):
    """Naive agent loop that only do single turn chat completion."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.prompt_length = self.rollout_config.prompt_length
        self.response_length = self.rollout_config.response_length

    @rollout_trace_op
    async def run(self, sampling_params: dict[str, Any], priority: int = 0, **kwargs) -> AgentLoopOutput:
        # priority may arrive as np.int64 from non_tensor_batch; normalize to Python int.
        priority = int(priority)
        messages = list(kwargs["raw_prompt"])

        # 1. extract multimodal inputs from messages
        multi_modal_data = await self.process_multi_modal_info(messages)
        images = multi_modal_data.get("images")
        videos = multi_modal_data.get("videos")
        audios = multi_modal_data.get("audios")
        mm_processor_kwargs = self._get_mm_processor_kwargs(audios)

        # 2. apply chat template and tokenize
        use_continuous_token = self.enable_continuous_token and not multi_modal_data
        if use_continuous_token:
            prompt_ids = await self.ct_build_initial_tokens(messages)
        else:
            prompt_ids = await self.apply_chat_template(
                messages,
                images=images,
                videos=videos,
                audios=audios,
                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
            )

        # 3. generate sequences
        metrics = {}
        with simple_timer("generate_sequences", metrics):
            request_id = f"det-{priority}" if getattr(self.rollout_config, "full_determinism", False) else uuid4().hex
            output: TokenOutput = await self.server_manager.generate(
                request_id=request_id,
                prompt_ids=prompt_ids,
                sampling_params=sampling_params,
                image_data=images,
                audio_data=audios,
                video_data=videos,
                mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
                priority=priority,
            )
        if metrics.get("num_preempted") is None:
            metrics["num_preempted"] = output.num_preempted if output.num_preempted is not None else -1

        if use_continuous_token:
            merge_result, response_mask, response_logprobs = await self.ct_merge_assistant_token(
                prompt_ids,
                output.token_ids,
                [],
                [] if output.log_probs else None,
                assistant_logprobs=output.log_probs if output.log_probs else None,
            )
            response_ids = merge_result.token_ids[-len(response_mask) :] if response_mask else []
            prompt_ids = merge_result.token_ids[: len(merge_result.token_ids) - len(response_mask)]
        else:
            response_ids = output.token_ids
            response_mask = [1] * len(output.token_ids)
            response_logprobs = output.log_probs

        output: AgentLoopOutput = AgentLoopOutput(
            prompt_ids=prompt_ids,
            response_ids=response_ids[: self.response_length],
            response_mask=response_mask[: self.response_length],
            response_logprobs=response_logprobs[: self.response_length] if response_logprobs else None,
            routed_experts=(
                output.routed_experts[: len(prompt_ids) + self.response_length]
                if output.routed_experts is not None
                else None
            ),
            multi_modal_data=multi_modal_data,
            mm_processor_kwargs=mm_processor_kwargs,
            num_turns=2,
            metrics=metrics,
            extra_fields=output.extra_fields,
        )

        # keeping the schema consistent with tool_agent_loop
        output.extra_fields.update({"turn_scores": [], "tool_rewards": []})

        return output

                f"model's maximum context length ({self.config.max_model_len}); need at least "

        if "max_tokens" in sampling_params:

            # support sglang-style 'max_new_tokens' param

1	# Full Determinism for Reproducible RL Training
2	
3	**Authors**: Haichuan Hu, Yongxiang Huang, Jiawei Zhang, Nguyen Long
4	
5	Last updated: 06/16/2026.
6	
7	## Overview
8	
9	By default, RL training in verl is **not** bitwise reproducible: identical configs run twice can produce different reward curves due to nondeterminism in GPU kernels, request scheduling, hash-based routing, and batch composition. The full determinism feature closes these gaps, enabling two identical runs to produce **bitwise-aligned reward curves**.
10	
11	Useful for:
12	
13	- **Debugging**: reproduce a training failure exactly, step-by-step
14	- **Regression testing**: verify that a code change has no silent effect on training outcomes
15	- **Research**: ensure fair comparison when evaluating algorithmic changes
16	
17	## Quick Start
18	
19	```yaml
20	actor_rollout_ref:
21	  rollout:
22	    full_determinism: true
23	    seed: 42
24	  actor:
25	    fsdp_config:
26	      full_determinism: true
27	  ref:
28	    fsdp_config:
29	      full_determinism: true
30	
31	reward:
32	  reward_model:
33	    enable: true
34	    rollout:
35	      full_determinism: true
36	      seed: 42
37	```
38	
39	Or via Hydra overrides:
40	
41	```bash
42	python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
43	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=true \
44	  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=42 \
45	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
46	  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
47	  reward.reward_model.enable=true \
48	  reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism=true \
49	  reward.reward_model.rollout.seed=42 \
50	  [other config overrides...]
51	```
52	
53	> **Important:** `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set **before the Python interpreter starts**. verl handles this automatically — it sets `PYTHONHASHSEED` from `rollout.seed` before `ray.init()` and propagates it to all Ray actors. Do NOT set it manually.
54	
55	## Configuration Reference
56	
57	| Parameter | Default | Scope | Description |
58	|-----------|---------|-------|-------------|
59	| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Rollout | Enables deterministic rollout generation |
60	| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed` | `42` | Rollout | Base seed; each replica uses `replica_rank + seed` |
61	| `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Actor | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for actor |
62	| `actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Ref model | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for reference model |
63	| `reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Reward model | Enables deterministic RM inference (forces `max_num_seqs=1`) |
64	| `reward.reward_model.rollout.seed` | `42` | Reward model | Base seed for RM vLLM server |
65	
66	## How It Works
67	
68	Determinism is enforced at five layers. All must be enabled for full E2E reproducibility:
69	
70	### PyTorch-level
71	
72	`enable_full_determinism(seed)` sets `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC`, seeds all RNGs, calls `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)`, and disables cuDNN benchmarking. Applied in all training engine implementations.
73	
74	### Environment propagation
75	
76	`main_ppo.run_ppo()` sets three env vars before `ray.init()`:
77	
78	- `PYTHONHASHSEED` — freezes Python hash() and dict ordering
79	- `VERL_FULL_DETERMINISM` — signals subprocesses to apply determinism
80	- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` — makes vLLM outputs independent of batch composition
81	
82	These are forwarded to all Ray actors via `PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV`.
83	
84	### vLLM batch invariance + per-request seed
85	
86	`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` ensures vLLM outputs don't depend on which other requests are batched together. Each `generate()` call injects `SamplingParams.seed = replica_rank + config.seed` to reset RNG per request.
87	
88	### Priority scheduling + deterministic routing
89	
90	Without determinism, request order depends on arrival timing and server selection on dict iteration order. When `full_determinism=true`:
91	
92	- Each sample gets a globally unique priority injected into the batch (`non_tensor_batch["priority"]`), so each rollout request is scheduled with a stable, distinct priority
93	- `SingleTurnAgentLoop` uses `request_id=f"det-{priority}"` instead of random UUID
94	- `GlobalRequestLoadBalancer` tie-breaking uses `hash(request_id) % len(candidates)` — deterministic with frozen `PYTHONHASHSEED`
95	
96	> **Note:** `priority` is a vLLM-only parameter. `LLMServerClient.generate()` automatically filters it for non-vLLM backends.
97	
98	### Reward model serialization
99	
100	vLLM's `/classify` endpoint (used by RM) does not support priority or batch invariance. When `full_determinism=true`, `RewardModelManager` forces `max_num_seqs=1`, serializing RM inference one request at a time.
101	
102	## Side Effects and Limitations
103	
104	**Performance**: deterministic PyTorch kernels are slower, cuDNN benchmarking is disabled, and RM `max_num_seqs=1` causes severe throughput loss. Typical E2E throughput drops 10–30% without RM; RM determinism can drop significantly more.
105	
106	**Recommendation**: Only enable for debugging, regression testing, or research. Leave disabled for production training.
107	
108	**Nondeterministic fallbacks**: Some GPU ops have no deterministic implementation. `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)` warns when these are encountered.
109	
110	**Backend support**:
111	
112	| Backend | Rollout | Reward model |
113	|---------|---------|--------------|
114	| vLLM | ✅ | ✅ (serialized) |
115	| SGLang | ❌ | ❌ |
116	| TensorRT-LLM | ❌ | ❌ |
117	
118	**PYTHONHASHSEED**: Must be set before process start. verl handles this automatically; manual Ray actor creation must propagate it via `runtime_env`.
119

# Full Determinism for Reproducible RL Training

**Authors**: Haichuan Hu, Yongxiang Huang, Jiawei Zhang, Nguyen Long

Last updated: 06/16/2026.

## Overview

By default, RL training in verl is **not** bitwise reproducible: identical configs run twice can produce different reward curves due to nondeterminism in GPU kernels, request scheduling, hash-based routing, and batch composition. The full determinism feature closes these gaps, enabling two identical runs to produce **bitwise-aligned reward curves**.

Useful for:

- **Debugging**: reproduce a training failure exactly, step-by-step
- **Regression testing**: verify that a code change has no silent effect on training outcomes
- **Research**: ensure fair comparison when evaluating algorithmic changes

## Quick Start

```yaml
actor_rollout_ref:
  rollout:
    full_determinism: true
    seed: 42
  actor:
    fsdp_config:
      full_determinism: true
  ref:
    fsdp_config:
      full_determinism: true

reward:
  reward_model:
    enable: true
    rollout:
      full_determinism: true
      seed: 42
```

Or via Hydra overrides:

```bash
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=true \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=42 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism=true \
  reward.reward_model.enable=true \
  reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism=true \
  reward.reward_model.rollout.seed=42 \
  [other config overrides...]
```

> **Important:** `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set **before the Python interpreter starts**. verl handles this automatically — it sets `PYTHONHASHSEED` from `rollout.seed` before `ray.init()` and propagates it to all Ray actors. Do NOT set it manually.

## Configuration Reference

| Parameter | Default | Scope | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Rollout | Enables deterministic rollout generation |
| `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed` | `42` | Rollout | Base seed; each replica uses `replica_rank + seed` |
| `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Actor | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for actor |
| `actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.full_determinism` | `false` | Ref model | Enables deterministic PyTorch ops for reference model |
| `reward.reward_model.rollout.full_determinism` | `false` | Reward model | Enables deterministic RM inference (forces `max_num_seqs=1`) |
| `reward.reward_model.rollout.seed` | `42` | Reward model | Base seed for RM vLLM server |

## How It Works

Determinism is enforced at five layers. All must be enabled for full E2E reproducibility:

### PyTorch-level

`enable_full_determinism(seed)` sets `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, `FLASH_ATTENTION_DETERMINISTIC`, seeds all RNGs, calls `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)`, and disables cuDNN benchmarking. Applied in all training engine implementations.

### Environment propagation

`main_ppo.run_ppo()` sets three env vars before `ray.init()`:

- `PYTHONHASHSEED` — freezes Python hash() and dict ordering
- `VERL_FULL_DETERMINISM` — signals subprocesses to apply determinism
- `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` — makes vLLM outputs independent of batch composition

These are forwarded to all Ray actors via `PPO_RAY_RUNTIME_ENV`.

### vLLM batch invariance + per-request seed

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` ensures vLLM outputs don't depend on which other requests are batched together. Each `generate()` call injects `SamplingParams.seed = replica_rank + config.seed` to reset RNG per request.

### Priority scheduling + deterministic routing

Without determinism, request order depends on arrival timing and server selection on dict iteration order. When `full_determinism=true`:

- Each sample gets a globally unique priority injected into the batch (`non_tensor_batch["priority"]`), so each rollout request is scheduled with a stable, distinct priority
- `SingleTurnAgentLoop` uses `request_id=f"det-{priority}"` instead of random UUID
- `GlobalRequestLoadBalancer` tie-breaking uses `hash(request_id) % len(candidates)` — deterministic with frozen `PYTHONHASHSEED`

> **Note:** `priority` is a vLLM-only parameter. `LLMServerClient.generate()` automatically filters it for non-vLLM backends.

### Reward model serialization

vLLM's `/classify` endpoint (used by RM) does not support priority or batch invariance. When `full_determinism=true`, `RewardModelManager` forces `max_num_seqs=1`, serializing RM inference one request at a time.

## Side Effects and Limitations

**Performance**: deterministic PyTorch kernels are slower, cuDNN benchmarking is disabled, and RM `max_num_seqs=1` causes severe throughput loss. Typical E2E throughput drops 10–30% without RM; RM determinism can drop significantly more.

**Recommendation**: Only enable for debugging, regression testing, or research. Leave disabled for production training.

**Nondeterministic fallbacks**: Some GPU ops have no deterministic implementation. `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)` warns when these are encountered.

**Backend support**:

| Backend | Rollout | Reward model |
|---------|---------|--------------|
| vLLM | ✅ | ✅ (serialized) |
| SGLang | ❌ | ❌ |
| TensorRT-LLM | ❌ | ❌ |

**PYTHONHASHSEED**: Must be set before process start. verl handles this automatically; manual Ray actor creation must propagate it via `runtime_env`.

**Data parallelism**: Each replica uses `replica_rank + seed`, producing different but internally reproducible outputs. Two runs with the same config produce bitwise-aligned results.

**Multi-turn agent not supported**: Full determinism only works for single-turn rollouts (`single_turn_agent_loop`). Multi-turn rollouts (`tool_agent_loop`) are **not** bitwise reproducible, for two reasons:

- `tool_agent_loop` uses a random UUID per trajectory as `request_id` and does not pass `priority` to `server_manager.generate()`, so the deterministic routing and priority scheduling described above do not apply.
- Even with those added, each turn is interleaved with external tool calls whose execution time varies across runs, so the order in which requests arrive at vLLM cannot be made deterministic. This is inherent to multi-turn agentic workloads.

For bitwise-reproducible rollouts, use `single_turn_agent_loop`. (The per-request sampling seed is still applied to multi-turn requests inside the vLLM server, but this alone is not sufficient for end-to-end reproducibility.)

## Verifying Determinism

Rollout determinism (bitwise reproducible vLLM generation):

```bash
VLLM_DETERMINISM_DENSE_MODEL_PATH=${HOME}/models/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
VLLM_DETERMINISM_N_GPUS=2 \
pytest tests/workers/rollout/rollout_vllm/test_vllm_generation_determinism.py -v -s
```

E2E training (bitwise-aligned reward curves across two full PPO runs):

```bash
python tests/experimental/reward_loop/run_determinism_e2e_with_rm.py \
  --policy_model ~/models/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --rm_model ~/models/Skywork/Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.2-1B \
  --train_files ~/data/gsm8k/train.parquet \
  --val_files ~/data/gsm8k/test.parquet \
  --n_gpus 2 --n_steps 5
```

class GlobalRequestLoadBalancer:
    """Global sticky-session + in-flight load balancer shared by all AgentLoopWorkers.

    When a sticky session points to a removed server, the cache entry is
    automatically invalidated and a new server is selected.

    Key features:
    - **Atomic acquire**: ``acquire_server()`` returns ``(server_id, handle)``
    - **Sticky Session**: Uses LRUCache to map request_id → server_id, ensuring
      multi-turn conversations route to the same server.
    - **Least-loaded Selection**: When no sticky session exists, selects the
      server with the fewest in-flight requests.
    - **Deterministic Routing**: When ``full_determinism=True``, tie-breaking
      among equally-loaded servers uses ``hash(request_id)`` so the same
      request always routes to the same server across runs.
    - **Dynamic Server Management**: Supports add/remove servers at runtime
      for hybrid scaling.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        servers: dict[str, ray.actor.ActorHandle],
        max_cache_size: int = DEFAULT_ROUTING_CACHE_SIZE,
        full_determinism: bool = False,
    ):
        if not servers:
            raise ValueError("servers must be non-empty")

        self._servers: dict[str, ray.actor.ActorHandle] = dict(servers)
        self._inflight_requests: dict[str, int] = {sid: 0 for sid in servers}
        self._request_id_to_server: LRUCache = LRUCache(maxsize=max_cache_size)
        self._full_determinism = full_determinism

    def acquire_server(self, request_id: str) -> tuple[str, ray.actor.ActorHandle]:
        """Acquire a server for the given request (sticky + least-loaded).

        Returns:
            A tuple of ``(server_id, actor_handle)`` in a single atomic call.
        """
        # Try sticky session first
        if request_id in self._request_id_to_server:
            server_id = self._request_id_to_server[request_id]
            # Check if server is still in the active pool
            if server_id in self._inflight_requests:
                self._inflight_requests[server_id] += 1
                return server_id, self._servers[server_id]
            # Server was removed, clear stale cache entry and re-select
            del self._request_id_to_server[request_id]

        # Select new server (least-loaded among available)
        if not self._inflight_requests:
            raise RuntimeError("No available servers in load balancer")

        min_count = min(self._inflight_requests.values())
        candidates = [sid for sid, count in self._inflight_requests.items() if count == min_count]
        if len(candidates) == 1:
            server_id = candidates[0]
        elif self._full_determinism:
            # Deterministic tie-breaking: same request_id → same server across runs
            server_id = candidates[hash(request_id) % len(candidates)]
        else:
            server_id = candidates[0]
        self._request_id_to_server[request_id] = server_id
        self._inflight_requests[server_id] += 1
        return server_id, self._servers[server_id]

    def release_server(self, server_id: str) -> None:
        """Release a server after a request completes."""
        if server_id not in self._inflight_requests:
            return
        if self._inflight_requests[server_id] > 0:
            self._inflight_requests[server_id] -= 1

@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_PASSK)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo_passk")
def compute_grpo_passk_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for Pass@k using a GRPO-style outcome reward formulation.
    Only the best response per group gets a non-zero advantage: r_max - r_second_max.

    Implemented as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19595.

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: (bs, response_length)
        index: (bs,) → group ID per sample
        epsilon: float for numerical stability
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm settings, which contains "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo"

    Returns:
        advantages: (bs, response_length)
        returns: (bs, response_length)
    """
    assert config is not None
    # if True, normalize advantage by std within group
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = config.get("norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True)
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)  # (bs,)
    advantages = torch.zeros_like(scores)

    id2scores = defaultdict(list)
    id2indices = defaultdict(list)

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            idx = index[i]
            id2scores[idx].append(scores[i])
            id2indices[idx].append(i)

        for idx in id2scores:
            rewards = torch.stack(id2scores[idx])  # (k,)
            if rewards.numel() < 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Pass@k requires at least 2 samples per group. Got {rewards.numel()} for group {idx}."
                )
            topk, topk_idx = torch.topk(rewards, 2)
            r_max, r_second_max = topk[0], topk[1]
            i_max = id2indices[idx][topk_idx[0].item()]
            advantage = r_max - r_second_max
            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
                std = torch.std(rewards)
                advantage = advantage / (std + epsilon)
            advantages[i_max] = advantage

    advantages = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
    return advantages, advantages

    """
    Vectorized GRPO（outcome-only）:
      For each group g:

        else:
            scalars = scores - mean_g[g]
        advantages = scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
        return advantages, advantages

                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

import re

_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300


def extract_solution(solution_str, method="strict"):
    assert method in ["strict", "flexible"]

    # Optimization: Regular expression matching on very long strings can be slow.
    # For math problems, the final answer is usually at the end.
    # We only match on the last 300 characters, which is a safe approximation for 300 tokens.
    if len(solution_str) > _SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:
        solution_str = solution_str[-_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:]

    if method == "strict":
        # this also tests the formatting of the model
        solutions = re.findall("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        if len(solutions) == 0:
            final_answer = None
        else:
            # take the last solution
            final_answer = solutions[-1].replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    elif method == "flexible":
        answer = re.findall("(\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        final_answer = None
        if len(answer) == 0:
            # no reward is there is no answer
            pass
        else:
            invalid_str = ["", "."]
            # find the last number that is not '.'
            for final_answer in reversed(answer):
                if final_answer not in invalid_str:
                    break
    return final_answer


def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
    """The scoring function for GSM8k.

    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.

    Args:
        solution_str: the solution text
        ground_truth: the ground truth
        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
        format_score: the score for the format
        score: the score for the correct answer
    """
    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
    if answer is None:
        return 0
    else:
        if answer == ground_truth:
            return score
        else:
            return format_score

15	import signal
16	from collections import defaultdict
17	from contextlib import contextmanager
18	from typing import Any, Optional
19	
20	import torch
21	
22	from verl import DataProto
23	from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
24	from verl.workers.reward_manager import register
25	from verl.workers.reward_manager.abstract import AbstractRewardManager
26	
27	
28	@contextmanager
29	def _score_timeout(seconds: Optional[float]):
30	    """Raise ``TimeoutError`` if the wrapped block runs longer than ``seconds``.
31	
32	    A single ``compute_score`` call on a pathological model output (e.g. a long,
33	    degenerate RL rollout that triggers catastrophic regex backtracking or a slow
34	    symbolic comparison) can run for a very long time. Because ``NaiveRewardManager``
35	    scores samples serially in the driver process, one such call blocks the entire
36	    training loop. This guard bounds the wall-clock time of each call.
37	
38	    Implemented with ``SIGALRM``, so it only takes effect on the main thread. If a
39	    handler cannot be installed (e.g. called from a non-main thread), it degrades to
40	    a no-op so reward computation still runs -- just without the timeout.
41	    """
42	    if not seconds or seconds <= 0:
43	        yield
44	        return
45	
46	    def _handler(signum, frame):
47	        raise TimeoutError(f"compute_score timed out after {seconds}s")
48	
49	    try:
50	        old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handler)
51	    except ValueError:
52	        # Not in the main thread -> SIGALRM is unavailable; run without a timeout.
53	        yield
54	        return
55	
56	    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
57	    try:
58	        yield
59	    finally:
60	        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
61	        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)
62	
63	
64	@register("naive")
65	class NaiveRewardManager(AbstractRewardManager):
66	    """The reward manager."""
67	
68	    def __init__(
69	        self, tokenizer, num_examine, compute_score=None, reward_fn_key="data_source", compute_score_timeout=None
70	    ) -> None:
71	        """
72	        Initialize the NaiveRewardManager instance.
73	
74	        Args:
75	            tokenizer: The tokenizer used to decode token IDs into text.
76	            num_examine: The number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console for debugging purpose.
77	            compute_score: A function to compute the reward score. If None, `default_compute_score` will be used.
78	            reward_fn_key: The key used to access the data source in the non-tensor batch data. Defaults to
79	                "data_source".
80	            compute_score_timeout: Optional per-sample timeout (in seconds) for `compute_score`. If set, a single
81	                scoring call that exceeds this limit is aborted, assigned a reward of 0.0, and training continues,
82	                instead of blocking the whole loop. Defaults to None (no timeout, unchanged behavior).
83	        """
84	        self.tokenizer = tokenizer  # Store the tokenizer for decoding token IDs
85	        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
86	        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
87	        self.reward_fn_key = reward_fn_key  # Store the key for accessing the data source
88	        self.compute_score_timeout = compute_score_timeout  # per-sample timeout (seconds) for compute_score
89	
90	    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor | dict[str, Any]:
91	        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""
92	
93	        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
94	        reward_from_rm_scores = self._extract_reward_from_rm_scores(data, return_dict)
95	        if reward_from_rm_scores is not None:
96	            return reward_from_rm_scores
97	
98	        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
99	        reward_extra_info = defaultdict(list)
100	
101	        already_print_data_sources = {}
102	
103	        for i in range(len(data)):
104	            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem
105	
106	            prompt_ids = data_item.batch["prompts"]
107	
108	            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]
109	
110	            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][:prompt_length].sum()
111	            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]
112	
113	            response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
114	            valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][prompt_length:].sum()
115	            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]
116	
117	            # decode
118	            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
119	            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
120	
121	            ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]
122	            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch[self.reward_fn_key]
123	            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("extra_info", {})
124	            num_turns = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("__num_turns__", None)
125	            rollout_reward_scores = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_scores", {})
126	            extra_info["num_turns"] = num_turns
127	            extra_info["rollout_reward_scores"] = rollout_reward_scores
128	
129	            try:
130	                with _score_timeout(self.compute_score_timeout):
131	                    score = self.compute_score(
132	                        data_source=data_source,
133	                        solution_str=response_str,
134	                        ground_truth=ground_truth,
135	                        extra_info=extra_info,
136	                    )
137	            except TimeoutError:
138	                print(
139	                    f"[NaiveRewardManager] compute_score exceeded "
140	                    f"{self.compute_score_timeout}s for data_source={data_source}; "
141	                    f"assigning reward 0.0 and continuing."
142	                )
143	                score = 0.0
144	
145	            if isinstance(score, dict):
146	                reward = score["score"]
147	                # Store the information including original reward
148	                for key, value in score.items():
149	                    reward_extra_info[key].append(value)
150	            else:
151	                reward = score
152	
153	            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = reward
154	
155	            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
156	                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0
157	
158	            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine:
159	                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
160	                print("[prompt]", prompt_str)
161	                print("[response]", response_str)
162	                print("[ground_truth]", ground_truth)
163	                if isinstance(score, dict):
164	                    for key, value in score.items():
165	                        print(f"[{key}]", value)
166	                else:
167	                    print("[score]", score)
168	
169	        if return_dict:
170	            return {
171	                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
172	                "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info,
173	            }
174	        else:
175	            return reward_tensor

import signal
from collections import defaultdict
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any, Optional

import torch

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
from verl.workers.reward_manager import register
from verl.workers.reward_manager.abstract import AbstractRewardManager


@contextmanager
def _score_timeout(seconds: Optional[float]):
    """Raise ``TimeoutError`` if the wrapped block runs longer than ``seconds``.

    A single ``compute_score`` call on a pathological model output (e.g. a long,
    degenerate RL rollout that triggers catastrophic regex backtracking or a slow
    symbolic comparison) can run for a very long time. Because ``NaiveRewardManager``
    scores samples serially in the driver process, one such call blocks the entire
    training loop. This guard bounds the wall-clock time of each call.

    Implemented with ``SIGALRM``, so it only takes effect on the main thread. If a
    handler cannot be installed (e.g. called from a non-main thread), it degrades to
    a no-op so reward computation still runs -- just without the timeout.
    """
    if not seconds or seconds <= 0:
        yield
        return

    def _handler(signum, frame):
        raise TimeoutError(f"compute_score timed out after {seconds}s")

    try:
        old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handler)
    except ValueError:
        # Not in the main thread -> SIGALRM is unavailable; run without a timeout.
        yield
        return

    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)


@register("naive")
class NaiveRewardManager(AbstractRewardManager):
    """The reward manager."""

    def __init__(
        self, tokenizer, num_examine, compute_score=None, reward_fn_key="data_source", compute_score_timeout=None
    ) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the NaiveRewardManager instance.

        Args:
            tokenizer: The tokenizer used to decode token IDs into text.
            num_examine: The number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console for debugging purpose.
            compute_score: A function to compute the reward score. If None, `default_compute_score` will be used.
            reward_fn_key: The key used to access the data source in the non-tensor batch data. Defaults to
                "data_source".
            compute_score_timeout: Optional per-sample timeout (in seconds) for `compute_score`. If set, a single
                scoring call that exceeds this limit is aborted, assigned a reward of 0.0, and training continues,
                instead of blocking the whole loop. Defaults to None (no timeout, unchanged behavior).
        """
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer  # Store the tokenizer for decoding token IDs
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
        self.reward_fn_key = reward_fn_key  # Store the key for accessing the data source
        self.compute_score_timeout = compute_score_timeout  # per-sample timeout (seconds) for compute_score

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor | dict[str, Any]:
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        reward_from_rm_scores = self._extract_reward_from_rm_scores(data, return_dict)
        if reward_from_rm_scores is not None:
            return reward_from_rm_scores

        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
        reward_extra_info = defaultdict(list)

        already_print_data_sources = {}

        for i in range(len(data)):
            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem

            prompt_ids = data_item.batch["prompts"]

            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]

            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][:prompt_length].sum()
            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]

            response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][prompt_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)

            ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]
            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch[self.reward_fn_key]
            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("extra_info", {})
            num_turns = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("__num_turns__", None)
            rollout_reward_scores = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_scores", {})
            extra_info["num_turns"] = num_turns
            extra_info["rollout_reward_scores"] = rollout_reward_scores

            try:
                with _score_timeout(self.compute_score_timeout):
                    score = self.compute_score(
                        data_source=data_source,
                        solution_str=response_str,
                        ground_truth=ground_truth,
                        extra_info=extra_info,
                    )
            except TimeoutError:
                print(
                    f"[NaiveRewardManager] compute_score exceeded "
                    f"{self.compute_score_timeout}s for data_source={data_source}; "
                    f"assigning reward 0.0 and continuing."
                )
                score = 0.0

            if isinstance(score, dict):
                reward = score["score"]
                # Store the information including original reward
                for key, value in score.items():
                    reward_extra_info[key].append(value)
            else:
                reward = score

            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = reward

            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0

            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
                print("[prompt]", prompt_str)
                print("[response]", response_str)
                print("[ground_truth]", ground_truth)
                if isinstance(score, dict):
                    for key, value in score.items():
                        print(f"[{key}]", value)
                else:
                    print("[score]", score)

        if return_dict:
            return {
                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
                "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info,
            }
        else:
            return reward_tensor

self, batch: DataProto, reward_extra_infos_dict: dict, timing_raw: dict, rollout_data_dir: str
    ):
        """Log rollout data to disk.
        Args:
            batch (DataProto): The batch containing rollout data
            reward_extra_infos_dict (dict): Additional reward information to log
            timing_raw (dict): Timing information for profiling
            rollout_data_dir (str): Directory path to save the rollout data
        """
        with marked_timer("dump_rollout_generations", timing_raw, color="green"):
            inputs = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(batch.batch["prompts"], skip_special_tokens=True)
            outputs = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(batch.batch["responses"], skip_special_tokens=True)
            scores = batch.batch["token_level_scores"].sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
            sample_gts = [item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in batch]

            reward_extra_infos_to_dump = {
                k: (v.tolist() if hasattr(v, "tolist") else v) for k, v in reward_extra_infos_dict.items()
            }
            if "request_id" in batch.non_tensor_batch:
                reward_extra_infos_to_dump.setdefault(
                    "request_id",
                    batch.non_tensor_batch["request_id"].tolist(),
                )

            self._dump_generations(
                inputs=inputs,
                outputs=outputs,
                gts=sample_gts,
                scores=scores,
                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_to_dump,
                dump_path=rollout_data_dir,
            )

    def _maybe_log_val_generations(self, inputs, outputs, scores):
        """Log a table of validation samples to the configured logger (wandb or swanlab)"""

        generations_to_log = self.config.trainer.log_val_generations

        if generations_to_log == 0:
            return

        import numpy as np

        # Create tuples of (input, output, score) and sort by input text
        samples = list(zip(inputs, outputs, scores, strict=True))
        samples.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])  # Sort by input text

        # Use fixed random seed for deterministic shuffling
        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
        rng.shuffle(samples)

        # Take first N samples after shuffling
        samples = samples[:generations_to_log]

        # Log to each configured logger
        self.validation_generations_logger.log(self.config.trainer.logger, samples, self.global_steps)

    def _get_gen_batch(self, batch: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        reward_keys = set({"data_source", "reward_model", "extra_info", "uid"}) & batch.non_tensor_batch.keys()

        # pop those keys for generation
        batch_keys_to_pop = []
        non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop = set(batch.non_tensor_batch.keys()) - reward_keys
        gen_batch = batch.pop(
            batch_keys=batch_keys_to_pop,
            non_tensor_batch_keys=list(non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop),
        )

        # For agent loop, we need reward model keys to compute score.
        gen_batch.non_tensor_batch.update(batch.non_tensor_batch)

steps.message: Let me verify the actual sampling params vLLM received (including the injected seed) and cross-step prompt/output identity, which together pin the mechanism.
steps.reasoning_content:
Now the full picture:

- The run completed all 30 steps cleanly ("Final validation metrics" printed; val at step 30 = 0.08719). The wandb-history.jsonl just wasn't flushed for the last steps (29, 30) — that's a truncated log artifact, not a defect. Task says: "A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect." Right.

- All 30 steps: `critic/advantages` mean/max/min = 0, `actor/grad_norm` = 0, `actor/pg_loss` = 0, `actor/loss` = 0, `actor/kl_loss` = 0, `actor/ppo_kl` = 0.

- Val acc frozen at exactly 0.087187 (115/1319) at steps 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

- Rollout dumps: all 8 samples per group are byte-identical outputs; rewards per group are all-0 or all-1.

So the run is UNHEALTHY: zero learning signal throughout.

Root cause chain: full_determinism mode injects a constant per-request sampling seed (`seed = replica_rank + config.seed` = 42 for the single replica) into every vLLM generate call, combined with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. With temperature=1.0 sampling, all n=8 samples of the same prompt get the same seed → identical token sequences → identical rewards within each GRPO group → group-relative advantage = (r − mean)/(std+ε) = 0 for every sample → pg_loss = 0, KL = 0 (policy never moves) → grad_norm = 0 → actor never updates (only tiny weight decay at lr 1e-6, wd 0.01 — negligible) → held-out val accuracy stays exactly at the base model's floor, and val generations are byte-identical across all evals (step 0, 15, 30 dumps identical).

Secondary observations to distinguish from root causes:
1. The low 8.7% val accuracy floor itself is a symptom — mostly of a format/reward mismatch: the reward manager uses strict GSM8K `#### <number>` extraction (verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py, `compute_score` with method="strict"), while Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (a chat model) often emits `\boxed{...}` instead (368/1319 vs 229/1319 with `####`). Even correct answers without `####` get 0 reward. This depresses the absolute reward level but is not the cause of the training failure — GRPO could still learn from all-0 vs all-1 groups if samples differed.

Hmm wait, actually, I should be careful here: is the format mismatch a "root cause" of anything? The run's failure is "no learning". The format mismatch just makes the base accuracy low and the reward signal sparse (~17% of groups have reward 1). If training worked, the model would learn the format. So it's a contributing condition to the low starting point but not the cause of the flat curve. I'll present it as a secondary factor, clearly distinguished.

2. Truncated wandb-history.jsonl (missing steps 29-30) — an artifact of offline wandb not flushing the final steps; the console history and train.log show the run completed all 30 steps with final validation. Not a defect.

3. Truncation: `data.truncation=error` and `response_length/clip_ratio=0` for all steps, `response/aborted_ratio=0`, prompt clip 0. No truncation issues. The `truncation=error` setting is unusual but did not trigger.

Now let me double-check the claim about the seed being the cause of identical samples, by checking the rollout files for within-group identical outputs and confirm that the outputs differ ACROSS prompts (yes obviously) and across steps for the same prompt if it appears twice (policy frozen but prompts differ across steps due to shuffling). Let me also verify a specific claim: that the same prompt appearing in two different steps' rollouts gets the same output (policy frozen + same seed → same output). Let me check overlap between rollouts/1.jsonl, 15.jsonl, 30.jsonl prompts.

That would be strong direct evidence of (a) frozen policy + (b) constant per-request seed producing the same output for the same prompt across steps.

Also, I want to verify the entropy metric varies across steps — entropy is computed on the actor's logits over the rollout batch; since each step samples different prompts, entropy varies. That's consistent.

One more check on the val seed: validation uses do_sample=False (greedy), so the identical val dumps across steps 0/15/30 are fully explained by the frozen policy (weights bit-identical after zero-grad updates? — well, weight decay does shrink weights by 1e-8 relative... let me think about whether that could change greedy outputs. 30 steps × lr(1e-6) × wd(0.01) = 3e-7 total relative weight shrink. Argmax flips from such tiny perturbations are extremely unlikely across 1319 samples; the byte-identical dumps confirm no flips occurred. Actually more precisely, AdamW with zero grad: exp_avg=0, exp_avg_sq=0, so update = -lr * wd * p exactly. So weights DID change slightly. But output unchanged.)

Wait, actually, I should double check: is grad truly exactly zero, or is it just rounded to 0? In wandb-history, grad_norm is 0.0 exactly. pg_loss 0.0, loss 0.0. advantages 0.0. If advantages are exactly zero (they are, by construction: r_i - mean = 0 for identical rewards), then pg_loss = Σ advantage × ratio = exactly 0. KL loss = KL(π‖π_ref) — if policy == ref exactly (bitwise), KL = 0 exactly. At step 1, policy == ref (no update yet). After a weight-decay-only update, KL would be tiny but nonzero... but it's reported as 0.0 at every step. Hmm, kl_loss at step 2..30 = 0.0 exactly. If weights changed by weight decay, KL would be nonzero (like 1e-9 or so, maybe reported as 0 due to underflow in bfloat16? loss dtype...). The KL is computed in float32 presumably; a 1e-8 relative weight change gives KL ~1e-16 maybe → 0.0. Fine, plausible.

Also — wait, actually I should double check whether the optimizer even steps when grad is zero. In FSDP, if all grads are zero, optimizer.step() still runs (grads exist, they're just zero — because the backward pass of a zero loss still produces zero grads, not None). Actually pg_loss = 0 → backward produces zero grads (multiplications by advantages). So yes, weight decay applies. Whatever — the point stands: no learning signal.

Let me also double-check the `training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr: 0.9996` and `rollout_corr/kl ~ 1e-4` — these are rollout-vs-training consistency diagnostics; they're healthy, so the failure isn't in weight sync or log-prob mismatch. Also `training/rollout_probs_diff_max ~0.09-0.15` — small differences between vLLM rollout logprobs and FSDP-computed logprobs; normal numerics. Good.

Another thing to verify: the advantages metric — in verl, `critic/advantages/*` comes from the computed advantages after `compute_advantage`. All zero. ✓.

Now, let me also confirm the exact seeding line one more time and check the config `rollout.seed=42` and `replica_rank=0`. In vllm_async_server.py line ~598: `sampling_params.setdefault("seed", self.replica_rank + self.config.seed)`. With n_gpus=1, replica_rank=0 → seed=42 for every request in every step. ✓

And in the single_turn_agent_loop, request_id = f"det-{priority}", priority unique per sample 0..511 → unique request IDs, so it's NOT a request-deduplication issue; the identical outputs come from identical seeds. ✓

Wait, but I should double check one thing — does vLLM dedupe requests with the same request_id? Not relevant since IDs are unique. But hmm, what about identical prompt + identical seed — could vLLM's "prefix caching" return identical outputs? Prefix caching only shares KV of prompt; sampling still uses per-request RNG. The cause is the seed. To be thorough: could there be another explanation for identical samples — e.g., temperature actually 0? Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user asked for a diagnosis of a staged post-training RL experiment located at `/user/user1/harbor-runs/e0b9064e28b8/workspace` (also visible as `/workspace`). Exact task requirements (verbatim constraints preserved):
   - "Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior."
   - "Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime, optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect."
   - "Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation interval are fixed."
   - Deliverable: "Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to: `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md`" (resolved to `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`).
   - "State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable files."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - verl GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) training with FSDP actor + vLLM rollout (colocated), Ray-based, single GPU
   - GRPO advantage: per-group (score − group_mean) / (group_std + 1e-6) → identically zero when all group rewards are equal (`verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py`, `@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO)` ~line 267)
   - verl full-determinism mode (`docs/advance/determinism.md`): `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=true` + `rollout.seed=42`; per-request `SamplingParams.seed = replica_rank + config.seed` injection; `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`; priority scheduling with unique per-sample priority; `request_id=f"det-{priority}"`; PYTHONHASHSEED propagation; documented as debug-only with 10–30% throughput cost
   - vLLM 0.17.0 per-request seeded sampling: identical prompt + identical seed → identical tokens (batch-invariant mode removes batch-composition dependence)

Interesting nuance. The installed vllm 0.17.0:
- `validate_environ` warns "Unknown vLLM environment variable detected: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT" — so `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is NOT in `environment_variables` (the registry in envs.py). Yet `vllm/config/vllm.py:1120` logs "Disabling cascade attention when VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT is enabled." So the var is read directly somewhere (probably via `os.environ.get("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT")`) in config/vllm.py and batch_invariant.py, not via the envs registry. So batch-invariant mode IS active (the config code checks it directly), while the registry just doesn't know about it — hence the harmless "unknown variable" warning. This is a mild upstream inconsistency, not causal for the run failure. Good — this resolves the apparent contradiction: the mechanism (batch-invariant mode) was active; the warning is a registry-mismatch cosmetic.

So my causal chain stands:
- run_grpo_fd.sh sets `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.full_determinism=True` and `rollout.seed=42`.
- vllm_async_server.py:~598 injects `SamplingParams.seed = replica_rank + config.seed = 0 + 42 = 42` for every generate request.
- With temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0 sampling, same prompt + same fixed seed + batch-invariant mode → all n=8 group members decode identically.
- Empirically proven: outputs/rollouts/{1,15,30}.jsonl show 64/64 groups with 8/8 character-identical outputs; reward patterns only all-0 or all-1 per group.
- GRPO: advantage = (r_i − mean_group)/std_group = 0 for every sample → actor/pg_loss = 0, kl_loss = 0 (KL between identical old/new logprobs), grad_norm = 0 at every one of the 30 steps (console-history.jsonl).
- Policy never updates → held-out eval frozen: val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 = 0.08718726307808947 at all 7 evals (steps 0,5,10,15,20,25,30); val_generations/{0,15,30}.jsonl outputs bit-identical (1319/1319).

Symptoms vs root causes:
- Root cause: constant per-request sampling seed (full_determinism mode) — every rollout request uses seed 42, collapsing within-group diversity.
- Symptoms: zero advantages/losses/grad_norm; flat, noisy training reward (0.06–0.27 driven purely by which prompts are sampled, since all-correct or all-incorrect groups); frozen validation accuracy.
- Contributing/secondary observations (not root causes): strict GSM8K "#### " regex extraction vs Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct's habitual \boxed{} answers depresses absolute accuracy floor (229/1319 contain "####" vs 368 containing \boxed; e.g. correct "18" answer in \boxed scored 0) — explains low level but not the freezing. wandb-history.jsonl ending at step 28 is an offline-flush artifact; console-history.jsonl has all 31 rows and train.log ends cleanly with "Final validation metrics" — not a truncation defect.
- Ruled out: log-prob mismatch (rollout_corr/kl ~1e-4, ppl_ratio ~1.0002, pearson ~0.9996); truncation (clip_ratio=0, aborted_ratio=0, max len 1020 < 1024, truncation=error never fired); reward manager mis-scoring (dumped scores match logged means); runtime failures (clean completion, ~28 s/step).
